title: planqc Expands into the UK with Double-Digit Million-Euro Cambridge Optical-Lattice Facility - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
German neutral-atom quantum computing company planqc has established a new UK subsidiary, planqc UK Ltd, backed by a double-digit million-euro investment to build an assembly, integration, and commissioning laboratory in Cambridge. Led by planqc co-founders Dr. Sebastian Blatt and Dr. Alexander Glätzle and supported by investor and board member Hermann Hauser, co-founder of Arm and Amadeus Capital Partners, the facility will house laser and optical subsystems and hire quantum hardware, error-correction, FPGA, and software engineers over the next two years.

In partnership with Professor Ulrich Schneider‘s group at the University of Cambridge’s Cavendish Laboratory, the Cambridge team will develop next-generation optical-lattice architectures that use overlapping laser beams to generate periodic trapping arrays capable of scaling neutral-atom processors toward millions of qubits. Following earlier expansion into Innsbruck, Austria, the UK site extends planqc’s European footprint—which now exceeds 130 employees and over €100 million in combined private funding and public contracts—toward financial and pharmaceutical users in London and Cambridge.
